New entry: rank #7, skill score 8.8 (Exceptional), +17% 12-1m momentum
New entry: rank #4, skill score 8.2 (Strong), +31% 12-1m momentum
New entry: rank #2, skill score 8.5 (Exceptional), +54% 12-1m momentum
New entry: rank #1, skill score 9.0 (Exceptional), +52% 12-1m momentum

why: It beat an equal-weight hold of the same 38 stocks in both halves of the test (24% vs 18% a year in 2012-18, 33% vs 27% in 2019-26). That is the fair comparison, because every stock in the test is a known survivor.
Trading once a quarter and keeping a holding while it stays in the top 8 cut costs to 0.8% a year.

Monthly 6-month momentum showed higher returns here, but cost about three times as much (2.5% a year), and fast, concentrated momentum gains the most from survivorship bias. The slower 12-month signal is the standard one in the research literature.
The 200-day trend filter did not improve results in this test, so it is off.
Expect deep falls: the chosen rules dropped 42% at their worst, against 33% for the index fund.
4 holdings keeps each position near 2,500 kr, large enough that the $1 minimum commission stays under 0.3% of a trade.
The skill's quality score cannot be backtested (no point-in-time fundamentals), so its value is measured live against the Momentum-only control.
